newsitem.title: UK: BA submits proposal in cabin crew dispute.
newsitem.headline: BA submits proposal in cabin crew dispute.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Thursday it had sent a proposal to arbitration service ACAS to try to settle its dispute with cabin crew as a strike deadline neared.

BA's cabin crew have threatened a three-day strike next week over plans to restructure pay and conditions, which are part of its goal of saving one billion pounds ($1.7 billion) by the end of the century.
Officials from the Transport & General Workers Unions say the package would cut cabin crew salaries and have bristled at BA sealing a deal with the smaller Cabin Crew 89 union.

A BA spokesman said the airline's proposal addressed two main concerns -- the union's fears about its members being worse off under the new arrangement, and the relationships between the two cabin crew unions.

"We hope that the proposals will be acceptable. This provides a way forward and we hope the unions will take this chance to sit down with us...We will await a response from ACAS and the TGWU and in the meantime it's business as usual," the spokesman said.
On Tuesday, BA offered arbitrated talks in an attempt to break the five-month deadlock and avert strikes which will hit the carrier in the busy -- and profitable -- summer season.
